recipes.name: Ragi Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients: 1/2 cup powdered organic jaggery or coconut sugar
1/4 cup cold-pressed melted coconut oil or melted ghee
2 to 3 tablespoons warm milk (dairy or almond milk)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together Ragi flour, cocoa powder, and baking soda.
In another bowl, whisk together melted ghee/coconut oil, powdered jaggery, and vanilla extract until smooth and free of clumps.
Combine the dry ingredients with the wet mixture. Gradually add 2-3 tablespoons of warm milk to bring the dough together into a soft, non-sticky dough.
Gently fold in the dark chocolate chips.
Roll into 10-12 lemon-sized balls, place them on the tray, and slightly flatten them with your palm or a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 12 to 15 minutes. The edges will look firm while the center remains slightly tender.
Remove and let them cool completely on a wire rack; they will crisp up beautifully as they cool.
recipes.baking_tip: Do not over-bake, as Ragi contains very little natural fat and will become dry or hard if baked beyond 16 minutes.

recipes.name: Jowar Banana Bread (Naturally Sweetened)
ingredients: 1/3 cup raw organic honey or maple syrup
2 large eggs (or 1/2 cup thick curd/flax egg for vegan substitute)
1/4 cup cold-pressed oil or melted butter
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a standard 8x4 inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, mash ripe bananas thoroughly with a fork.
Add honey, eggs (or curd), melted butter/oil, and whisk until fully blended.
In a separate bowl, sift Jowar flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture using a spatula until just combined. Fold in chopped walnuts.
Pour batter evenly into the greased loaf pan and smooth the top.
Bake at 175°C for 40 to 45 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center emerges clean.
Allow to cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire cooling rack before slicing.
recipes.baking_tip: Jowar lacks gluten, so handle gently when warm. It pairs wonderfully with a thin spread of almond or peanut butter.

recipes.name: Bajra Jeera Mathri (Savory Tea-Time Crackers)
ingredients: 1/4 cup whole wheat flour or roasted gram flour (besan) for binding
Warm water as required to knead
instructions: In a mixing vessel, combine Bajra flour, gram flour, cumin, black pepper, ajwain, and rock salt.
Rub the warm desi ghee into the flour mix with your fingertips until it resembles breadcrumbs (this ensures crispness).
Gradually sprinkle warm water and knead into a stiff, firm dough. Rest covered for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F).
Divide dough into small round balls. Flatten each ball with your palm and prick all over with a fork so they do not puff during baking.
Arrange on a baking sheet and bake at 160°C for 18 to 22 minutes, turning them once halfway through until crispy and golden brown.
Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.
recipes.baking_tip: Pricking with a fork is mandatory to maintain the flat, crisp cracker texture.

recipes.name: Traditional Ragi Malt (Energizing Porridge Drink)
ingredients: 1 cup milk (or warm water for vegan/dairy-free version)
Pinch of grated nutmeg or roasted almond slivers (optional)
instructions: In a small saucepan, whisk 2 tablespoons of Ragi flour with 1/2 cup room-temperature water until completely smooth without any lumps.
Place the saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously with a whisk to prevent lumps or sticking to the bottom.
Once the mixture turns glossy, thick, and dark brown, pour in the warm milk and whisk vigorously.
Simmer for another 1-2 minutes until you achieve a smooth drinking consistency.
Turn off the flame, stir in the powdered jaggery and cardamom powder until dissolved.
Pour into a mug, garnish with almond slivers, and serve warm.
recipes.baking_tip: Never mix dry Ragi flour directly into hot liquids; always dissolve it in room-temperature liquid first to avoid lump formation.

recipes.name: Foxtail Millet Vegetable Khichdi
ingredients: 1 cup Foxtail Millet (washed and soaked for 30 minutes)
1/2 cup yellow moong dal (split yellow lentils)
1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, french beans)
1 teaspoon cumin seeds, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric, 1 teaspoon garam masala
1 tablespoon ghee, 4.5 cups water, salt to taste
instructions: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds, grated ginger, and green chilies.
Sauté onions until translucent, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add mixed vegetables, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the soaked and drained foxtail millet and moong dal. Mix gently.
Add 4.5 cups of water. Close the pressure cooker lid and cook for 3 whistles on medium flame (or simmer covered in a pot for 20-25 minutes).
Let the steam release naturally. Open, stir in a spoonful of ghee, and serve hot with curd or roasted papad.
recipes.baking_tip: Soaking foxtail millet for 30 minutes makes the grain tender, fluffy, and significantly easier to digest.
